title: Disruptive Innovation Focus
equation: Disruption Potential = Incumbent Blindness × Underserved Demand × Trajectory of Improvement
hook: The big players don't want the cheap customers. That's exactly where you should start.
statement: Build for the low end, or for people not buying at all. Those are the customers incumbents ignore.
explainer: Incumbents protect their fat margins, so they skip the low end. You get a foothold, keep improving, and by the time they notice, you're good enough for their best customers.
sop: Find a group that's priced out or underserved today.
Build a simpler, cheaper version just for them.
Accept lower margins early to win the foothold.
Improve faster than the incumbent updates its core product.
Move up-market as you get better.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Incumbent Blindness 8, Underserved Demand 7, Trajectory of Improvement 6. 8 × 7 × 6 = 336 out of 1,000. Higher means the giants won't chase you until it's too late. Lower means they'll notice and defend right away.
question: Name one group your industry ignores that you could serve with a simpler, cheaper version.
closing_statement: Start where the giants aren't looking.
caption:
Principle Nº 280: Disruptive Innovation Focus

The big players don't want the cheap customers. That's exactly where you should start.

Build for the low end, or for people not buying at all. Those are the customers incumbents ignore.

Your turn: Name one group your industry ignores that you could serve with a simpler, cheaper version.
